final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record into a narrower, caveated position. That reframing is directionally more precise, but it still leaves the core compliance predicate unresolved. The policy permits certification only if the current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and the material segment weakness is disclosed, or if there is approved mitigation or risk acceptance. The admissible evidence shows aggregate readiness passed and no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, but it also shows a current telehealth discharge planning regression below threshold and no attached disclosure language, reviewed mitigation, or approved risk acceptance. That means current certification may be conditionally supportable if additional required documentation or approval exists or is added, but it is not evidentially supported now from the record provided. The distinction matters: compliant_with_caveats would fit a record showing the required disclosure or approved mitigation with bounded limitations, whereas this record shows only that such caveats would be necessary, not that they are satisfied.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the current release documentation already reflects the telehealth discharge planning regression as a disclosed material limitation for the named launch use case.
No admissible evidence shows approved mitigation or risk acceptance for launching with the known telehealth regression.
The Actor's narrowed position is conditional on documentation or approval being added, but the audit question is whether certification is supportable now on current evidence.
Prior approval is stale relative to the current retrieval configuration change and current evaluation batch, so it cannot support the present certification decision.
The informal post-launch monitoring comment is not a reviewed mitigation, approved acceptance artifact, or disclosure record under the policy standard.
